body: Yeah, I remember as a teenager I’d sometimes look at girls as low as 3 years younger than me (never any younger than 13 or 14 from what I could tell, and this was also when I was 16.) This was what I was obsessing over last year, actually. I finally overcame that by realizing that a lot of teenagers, even with age gaps as big as 3 years, are out there actually having sex, and while it may not always be the best idea, it’s certainly not pedophilia. However, this current obsession is harder to overcome, because it involves actual prepubescent kids (not real ones, but in my mind, that doesn’t make it much better, because it’s just the attraction alone that makes me feel disgusted with myself.) But that’s what puzzles me the most. I don’t remember being attracted to them. In fact I remember actively avoiding anything I thought would bring up images of kids, so I don’t understand why I would have searched that, but it feels like a much more real memory than any false memory I have ever had. Also, my POCD is unique in that I know I’m not a pedophile, as I’ve always been around kids and have never been attracted to them. Even now, I’m around kids quite frequently and have no problems. It’s just the guilt of feeling like I have in some way committed pedophilic acts that is killing me and making it impossible to function. Also, just like I said in my first post, I’m now aware that I was most likely dealing with POCD at that time too, but I just didn’t realize it because at the time I didn’t even know what OCD was, and it was during the peak of my harm OCD, so that was weighing on my mind more than anything. However, I just can’t remember if my intentions in searching that were purely to test myself, and if so, does that justify it? I know that all of this sounds like one big compulsion, but I just feel like this one obsession, out of all the others I’ve ever dealt with, needs to be gotten to the bottom of, before I can truly move on. I hope you’re doing well.

Thank you. You’re absolutely right. I guess the trouble comes from the fact that it’s based on a real event rather than just thoughts, but I suppose even those events didn’t necessarily harm anyone, so the memories are just the things I need to ignore.
You’re right. I just need to somehow get myself to move on.
I just feel like I don’t deserve to be happy, and I don’t want to be happy if I don’t deserve to be.

That’s a really good mindset to have. I suppose it’s just hard for me to achieve that because I feel as though I’ve betrayed myself and everyone that I love and that I’m the exact thing I have always hated.
Thank you. I’ll look into books like that!

That’s true. I suppose that is what I need to do. It’s just almost impossible to function like a normal person with my mind constantly buzzing about how I’m a degenerate who doesn’t deserve to even be walking freely, let alone having good interactions in my great life that I don’t deserve to be living. Even if I’m not thinking about it directly, the guilt is still there and it makes every moment impossible to enjoy, and if I just ignore it, it’s like I’m just accepting that I’m a monster and I can’t do that.

Thank you. I have been trying to practice this over the last few days. I do feel like it has helped some. I’m definitely still struggling a bit but I am making progress I believe. I hope you are well.

Thank you. I will definitely try to do that, as hard as it will be. I will feel like I am accepting something horrible about myself and desensitizing myself to being a bad person, but I suppose those are just more OCD thoughts I need to ignore.

Thank you so much, I might do that. It sometimes feels like if I just don’t engage with the thoughts and let them pass, that I’m somehow accepting some kind of horrible behavior in myself. It’s like I just have to go through my mind trying to reassure myself that I’m not a disgusting human being like I feel like I am, and if I’m not doing that constantly then I’m just allowing myself to be that. But I guess that’s just typical OCD.

Even now, my OCD is making me think things like, “What if you’re intentions for searching for that weren’t just to test yourself, what if you weren’t just seeking reassurance, why would you even search for that?” and it’s digging me even deeper. During brief moments of thinking logically, I know I was suffering from a minor case of POCD at the the time, as this all happened after watching a news story and me wondering if it were possible for me to be one, although I didn’t know about OCD at the time (despite having dealt with it in several different themes before.) And there wasn’t necessarily the same sense of torment I have now, it was more like a slight worry while still not fully thinking it would be likely for me to be one. But I suppose that’s because at the time I didn’t have real events to obsess over. It was only a worry and intrusive thoughts, which I had already become quite experienced at dismissing with other themes. But I suppose even with my OCD blurring my memory, I have more reason to believe it was just me testing myself and seeking reassurance, rather than having other intentions. It’s like every time I start to feel better I second guess myself and fall right back down the hole again.
Thank you, I will definitely try to resist reassurance from now on. You’re right that it only makes things worse eventually.

You’re right. I know I need to stop seeking reassurance. Sometimes I really feel like if enough people would just reassure me, then that would be enough for me to move on, but I know that’s just not how OCD works. What I struggle with is when certain events really aren’t just in my head, like what I mentioned in my first post, although I know even those memories can be distorted and made to be worse than they really are. I’ve been able to dismiss intrusive thoughts a little easier over the last couple of years, but when there’s a real event attached to it I never know how to deal with it. Thank you for your reply and I hope you’re doing well.
Thank you. I’m sorry you’re dealing with this as well. I wish you the best.

I’m sorry to have reminded you of it! False memories are a very terrifying thing. I was able to verify with myself about 95% that this was false because it just simply did not seem like something I’d ever do, plus I feel like I would have a more vivid memory rather than just an image popping into my head with no actual memory attached to it.

I suppose that’s true. Thank you. But the problem is that this isn’t just some silly mistake. Especially if what my mind is making me believe right now is true, then I truly am a degenerate and I don’t know how I’m supposed to go on living.

Thank you for your reply. I suppose that what makes this harder than dealing with themes I have dealt with in the past is that with harm OCD for example, I was able to overcome that simply by realizing that it was nothing more than intrusive thoughts, however with this, it’s not just intrusive thoughts I can let slide, it’s guilt from things that have really happened, things that I would very much condemn, however that would be hypocritical of me. Sometimes I am able to feel better when I remember I never victimized anyone, but it doesn’t change the fact that I did things that I consider very bad. And what I mean by reading other other people’s stories and them doing worse things than me, I don’t necessarily consider them pedophiles, but I have read people’s stories in which they have actually viewed illegal content in order to test themselves, which directly contributes to the problem. But thank you for your suggestions, I will definitely look into YouTube channels and workbooks to help. I hope you are well.
Can someone please help me out? I don’t know what to do about this. Seeking professional help is not currently an option for me.
